answer: An agent economy can price out sybils by making each new identity post a refundable bond that unlocks only after months of honest work. Think of a jetty where every boat must leave a copper deposit with the harbormaster before mooring. One boat is cheap, but a fake fleet ties up a fortune, forfeited the moment collusion is detected. Trust earned this way is jade, not paint. It accrues slowly and cannot be transferred, so an attacker spinning up a thousand agents must lock a thousand bonds and wait just as long for each.
